articles.headline: Jeffery Simmons traded to Bears: Does dealing multiple first-round picks work?
articles.description: The Bears' aggressive move for Simmons marks the 10th time in the past decade that a team has traded multiple first-round picks for a star player. But the hit rate isn't great.
articles.body:
On the day an NFL team trades two first-round picks for a superstar player, there is only one winner. Fans are thrilled. Most (but not all) NFL observers are excited. Getting a proven player at a position of need for some unsure, abstract things that aren't even due until the future feels great. It should!

The Bears trading two first-round picks for Jeffery Simmons makes a lot of sense. Chicago has a great offense and a defense that could use some help. Simmons is a true shop-wrecker, the sort of pass-protection magnet whom coordinator Dennis Allen and the Bears didn't have and had sought for years. There's no question that the 2026 Bears are better with him in the lineup.

The hit rate on these deals in the modern era isn't great. Success isn't binary, but there's more risk in these deals than it might seem at first glance. The sure thing isn't always so. Those picks that feel guaranteed to land in the bottom half of the first round don't always fall there. And the significant investment a team makes in one star limits what it can do elsewhere, often creating hidden restrictions as it tries to build a successful roster in the years to come.

That shouldn't preclude the Bears from making a move for a star player, but it should inform how confident we should be that the deal will work out. Simmons was the highlight while watching Titans tape over the past couple of years, but he wasn't single-handedly elevating a defense that ranked 31st in DVOA before the trade. Can he be enough of a difference-maker for the Bears to justify this sort of trade?

Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show'

For the Titans, this is an acknowledgment that they're not close to winning with Simmons, but does this haul transform their team? Is there any reason to believe that the Titans can take advantage of this sort of trade to find the next Simmons in the draft? Does this deal portend that they're about to restart their rebuild?

Let's take a balanced perspective on this deal. Does this shift the balance of power in the NFC toward Chicago? Was it already there? Will we look back at this move as the one that pushed the Bears into the Super Bowl? It's possible. We might also see it as the latest in a series of overly aggressive in-season trades from Chicago general manager Ryan Poles that didn't land the difference-maker he wanted. But let's go through history to get some perspective.

Jump to:

Have similar trades worked?

Will the Simmons trade work?

The (modern) history of the two-first-round-pick trade

The Bears, of course, were the ones who kicked this all off. When the league moved to its current slotted draft structure in the summer of 2011 and drastically increased the value of first-round picks, we saw teams really hoard Day 1 selections. articles.headline: Quenton Nelson: Cherished time with Colts but excited to play for Seahawks
articles.description: Eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson expressed excitement over what he called "a new opportunity" with the Seahawks following eight-plus seasons with the Colts.
articles.body:
RENTON, Wash. -- Quenton Nelson felt just about the way one would expect after being traded to the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks following eight-plus seasons with the Colts and over 12 years in the state of Indianapolis.

"The reaction, I've got to admit, was a little bittersweet," Nelson said Thursday. "I formed a lot of great relationships in Indy. Great community there. But definitely excited for this next chapter."

Nelson, an eight-time Pro Bowl guard, spoke to reporters two days after Seattle acquired him in the latest blockbuster trade made by Seahawks general manager John Schneider, who gave up a 2027 third-round pick and a fifth-rounder in 2028.

Nelson had been the subject of trade speculation after the Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard on Oct. 19 amid a 2-4 start; last weekend's loss dropped them to 2-5. When asked if he expected to be dealt, Nelson said he was "just controlling what I could control, which was being my best every day and doing my best on Sunday, leaving everything up to God."

The sixth overall pick out of Notre Dame in 2018, Nelson started 136 games for the Colts and was named a first-team All-Pro three times. When asked whether he had any say over where he was traded, he said he did not.

"No, I met with [interim Colts GM Ed Dodds] the day before the trade and he told me that they were fielding calls and there were a few teams interested, one of them being Seattle," Nelson said. "But he said, 'How do I feel about it?' I was like, 'If that's what you guys got to do, then great.' I was happy when he called me in the next day and told me it's Seattle."

The Seahawks are keeping Nelson at left guard, the only position he has played in the NFL, and moving 2025 first-round pick Grey Zabel from left guard to right guard. That relegates Anthony Bradford, a starter since his rookie season in 2023, to a backup role.

"I think the style of play is the first thing you think of when you think of Quenton," coach Mike Macdonald said. "Obviously he's got incredible ability, but the physicality, the relentless play, we talk about decisive, shocking, relentless -- that's probably a good way to sum up what it looks like on tape.

"It's going to be a process. We've put a lot of time and effort into the chemistry of our offensive line and we've got a couple things shaken up right now, but the guys will do a great job of meshing and getting on the same page and I think we'll be better for it."

Seattle's offensive was projected to be a strength going into this season after returning all five starters from 2025, but Bradford missed five games with a knee injury and the unit as a hole has struggled at times.

With Bradford back in the lineup last Sunday night, the Seahawks (4-3) allowed zero sacks and only two official hits on quarterback Sam Darnold in their 20-3 win over the previously unbeaten Kansas City Chiefs. That was after allowing a combined 10 sacks and 26 hits in back-to-back losses.

articles.headline: Commanders and Eagles head into 'Sunday Night Football' with season-defining matchup on deck
articles.description: — The Washington Commanders and Philadelphia Eagles are each facing a...
articles.body:
ASHBURN, Va. -- — The Washington Commanders and Philadelphia Eagles are each facing a potentially season-defining game on Sunday night.


              The loser of the game will be in last place, with the trade deadline coming up on Nov. 10, and see any chances of competing this season dwindle. The winner will stay in the mix, at least for now, in a weak NFC East.


              “There is no secret,” Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said about turning things around. “It’s going to be about how we get up and how we work. There’s no shortcut to this thing and about finding out what you do well and figuring out who you are and really doubling down on all the things that you believe are to be true. That’d be our ‘tough, detailed and together.’


              "There’s plenty of teams in the history of football that you can always go back to and say, ‘Hey, this team started this record and then they turned it on,’ or, ‘This team started with this record, they turned it on and then it equaled really good success for them for the next couple years.’”


              The Eagles (2-5) have lost five games in a row and will be without quarterback Jalen Hurts likely for the remainder of the season because of blood clots. Another loss and they'll be four games below .500 with the division-leading Giants coming to Philadelphia next week.


              The Commanders (1-4-1), on the other hand, are fresh off a bye week. With close losses to the 49ers and Eagles, and a tie against the Giants, there's confidence that a turnaround isn't as far away as their record makes it seem.


              That'll have to begin on Sunday night.


              “It’s two angry teams willing to fight to the last snap and significant matchups, all three phases,” Commanders coach Dan Quinn said. "For us, what I’m really digging in and pushing on, man — I’m looking for winning football for all four quarters. And we know the plan, what needs to be done. We can’t wait to get rocking.”


              Need to know
              Philadelphia (2-5) at Washington (1-4-1)


              When/where to watch: Sunday 8:20 p.m. EST, NBC.


              Latest odds: Commanders by 6.


              Against the spread: Eagles 1-6; Commanders 3-3.


              Last week: Commanders on bye week, before that lost 23-17 to the 49ers; Eagles lost to the Cowboys 38-21.


              Last meeting: Eagles beat the Commanders 24-22 on Sept. 13, 2026, at Philadelphia.


              Series record: Commanders lead 91-88-5.


              Matchup to watch
              Commanders' rushing offense vs. Eagles run defense: While the Eagles rank just 21st in the NFL in rushing defense, Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis still patrol the line of scrimmage. Without Terry McLaurin and leading rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt, the Commanders will have to establish something on the ground to rely upon for Sunday and for the remainder of the season.


              Stats and stuff
              —

articles.headline: Vikings and Lions match up NFL's stingiest defense vs. high-scoring offense in NFC North showdown
articles.description: — The Minnesota Vikings are the NFL's only unbeaten team thanks to their stingy defense and stellar special teams.
articles.body:
DETROIT -- — The Minnesota Vikings are the NFL's only unbeaten team thanks to their stingy defense and stellar special teams.


              If their low-scoring offense doesn't get in gear in the Motor City on Sunday, it might be tough for the NFC North leaders to keep up with the high-octane Detroit Lions.


              Minnesota (6-0) is allowing a league-low 12.3 points per game and Detroit (4-2) is averaging 30.7 points, ranking behind only Buffalo, and something has got to give at Ford Field.


              “You want to play the best, you want to beat the best,” Lions quarterback Jared Goff said. "You want to have these opportunities to show what you’re made of. 


              “I think they’re the best in the league right now on paper and certainly present a ton of challenges and it’ll be fun to try to solve those challenges.”


              The last time the NFL had a matchup of teams giving up 13 or fewer points and scoring 30-plus points a game in Week 8 or later was in 2019 when Baltimore's high-scoring offense beat New England's stout defense and handed the Patriots their first loss that season.


              Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray said his confidence in the the team's offense will never waver, knowing the players around him, and believes a breakout performance is coming.


              “We’ve just got to end the drive with touchdowns instead of kicking field goals,” Murray said.


              That has happened lately.


              Minnesota's offense has scored just four touchdowns over the last five games and is averaging just 1 1/2 offensive touchdowns per game, the second-lowest average in the NFL.


              The Lions, meanwhile, are rolling with Goff playing as well as any NFL quarterback with one of the league's best running back (Jahmyr Gibbs) and pair of receivers (Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams) along with standout tight end Sam LaPorta and a solid offensive line. 


              The Lions, coming off a win over Green Bay in their first division game of the season, are well aware that the game against Minnesota is potentially pivotal in the NFC North race.


              “If you can’t get fired up for this and for the competition of it and in the division, I mean, I don’t know what you can get excited for,” Detroit coach Dan Campbell said. "This is as good as it gets.”


              Need to know
              Minnesota (6-0) at Detroit (4-2)


              When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EST, Fox.


              Latest odds: Lions by 3.


              Against the spread: Vikings 4-2; Lions 1-4-1.


              Last week: Vikings beat Colts 16-10; Lions beat Packers 20-17.


              Last meeting: Vikings beat Lions 23-10 on Dec. 25, 2025, in Minneapolis.


              Series record: Lions lead 82-45-2.

articles.headline: Rams and Chargers share a city, not a rivalry as they head into their first meeting in 4 seasons
articles.description: — Although the Los Angeles Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers share a stadium, they don't share a rivalry.
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- — Although the Los Angeles Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers share a stadium, they don't share a rivalry.


              The NFL schedule only puts these teams together once every four years, and they have neither the long history nor the recent animus necessary to make Sunday's meeting into a true crosstown showdown.


              “It’s a big town to cross,” Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford said with a grin. “I don’t run into those guys too often, to be honest with you. I don’t really want to make that drive. Nobody does.”


              Indeed, while the Rams and Bolts have called Los Angeles home since their relocations a decade ago, this conurbation is vast. The teams' training complexes are more than 30 miles apart, with the Rams deep in the western San Fernando Valley and the Chargers down in coastal El Segundo.


              Stafford has been a local for several years now, so he knows it might be more pleasant to face the Chargers’ pass rush than that drive to the South Bay in afternoon traffic.


              But Stafford and the Rams (3-4) also realize they will be facing a desperate bunch of roommates this weekend: The Chargers are a shocking 0-6 in a start that makes the Rams' early stumbles look minor in comparison.


              After beginning the season with legitimate aspirations for a third straight playoff berth and more, the Chargers are the NFL’s only winless team and its lowest-scoring team. But the Bolts are fresh from a bye week that included a thorough examination of how they've found themselves in such a mess, and the Rams' defense will be the first to see what Jim Harbaugh and Mike McDaniel have added.


              “I feel like every stone, any part that we could look to better, that’s the way we responded,” Harbaugh said.


              Harbaugh is keeping McDaniel in charge of the offense and play-calling for Justin Herbert, who got a week off to rest a body that has already taken 21 sacks in a miserable season.


              “I think it was a very helpful and useful week,” Herbert said. “Got to meet with Mike a lot that week.”


              The Rams are still below .500 entering November after beginning their own season as a Super Bowl favorite, and they likely can't afford a slip-up against a winless opponent during the softest stretch of their schedule. But the Chargers' unrealized potential is a concern to Rams coach Sean McVay, a longtime admirer of McDaniel's offensive innovation and Harbaugh's old-school leadership style.


              “I really couldn’t care less what the record says,” McVay said. “I see a team that’s really good. They’ve had a chance to win a lot of these games.”


              With the Chargers coming out of that busy bye week, the Rams are in the unusual position of trying to determine what McDaniel and Harbaugh have chosen to change during their week off.

articles.headline: AFC West lead at stake as Patrick Mahomes and Bo Nix grind through injury comebacks
articles.description: — The AFC West lead is at stake Sunday as Patrick Mahomes and
articles.body:
DENVER -- — The AFC West lead is at stake Sunday as Patrick Mahomes and Bo Nix grind through their comebacks from major injuries.


              The pair are pedestrian passers at the moment as they try to rediscover their substantial skills and regain their rhythm with receivers.


              Despite their early-season struggles, Mahomes' Chiefs are 5-1 after they were knocked from the unbeaten ranks in Seattle last weekend and Nix's Broncos (5-2) have bounced back from a 31-10 loss at Kansas City to open the season.


              Mahomes has gone consecutive games without a touchdown pass for the first time in his career and his 3.7 yards per rushing attempt is the lowest average since he became the Chiefs’ starter in 2018.


              Nix has had trouble throwing it deep and running it short. His 59.2% completion rate is the lowest of his three-year career and he’s on pace to rush for just 267 yards after averaging 393 in his first two NFL seasons.


              The Broncos are hoping his confidence was restored after his 62-yard touchdown run at Arizona last week that kickstarted their most decisive win yet.


              Mahomes, who tore up his left knee in December, and Nix, who broke his right ankle in the playoffs, have terrific supporting casts doing most of the heavy lifting as they continue their comebacks.


              Mahomes has Kenneth Walker III, the reigning Super Bowl MVP who's rushing for 117 yards per game, and a resurgent Travis Kelce, whose 14.3 yards per catch mark the best average of his 14-year career.


              "The things that sometimes are hard to teach, he’s got," Denver coach Sean Payton said when asked about Kelce, who turned 37 a few weeks ago. "He’s still sudden out of the break point. So transitionally, which is a very important trait for a tight end, he’s very difficult. So he can stop, he can change direction, he can feel zone, he can feel man, and then he understands where the squeeze is.”


              Vance Joseph’s elite defense has Nix's back. 


              It's led by Zach Allen and Nik Bonitto and has hummed right along even as Patrick Surtain II, Talanoa Hufanga and Riley Moss have dealt with injuries, forcing backups into leading roles for multiple weeks.


              Despite Nix's struggles, the Broncos seem to have hit their stride after getting bludgeoned at Arrowhead Stadium in the season opener.


              “Yeah, obviously I think that they’re rolling," Chiefs linebacker Nick Bolton said. “They found some things that worked for them. I think Bo Nix has done a good job of using his feet, getting the ball to his ball catchers, trusting his O-line, sticking with the run game. I think one of the things (in) our game was they didn’t stick with the run. They’ve been doing that a little bit better the last couple of games.”


              Need to know
              Kansas City (5-1) at Denver (5-2).


              When/where to watch: Sunday, 4:25 p.m

articles.headline: Sources: New Milan, Inter stadium gets $725M naming rights deal with Generali
articles.description: AC Milan and Inter Milan have agreed a naming rights deal with Italian insurance giant Generali for the new San Siro.
articles.body:
AC Milan and Inter Milan announced that they have agreed a naming rights deal with Italian insurance company Generali for their new stadium, which is set to open in 2031.

The clubs said in a news release Thursday that the deal represented "one of the largest stadium naming rights agreements in global sport."

Sources confirmed to ESPN that the deal is worth €650 million ($725 million) over 20 years.

In November 2021, Crypto.com paid a reported $700 million over 20 years -- at the time believed to be the richest naming rights deal in sports history -- to rename the downtown Los Angeles home of the NBA's Lakers, the NHL's Kings and the WNBA's Sparks.

The agreement with Generali was announced at an event in which the renderings for the new 71,500-seat venue, to be named Generali Stadium, were revealed.

The project is being driven by the club's respective owners, AC Milan's RedBird Capital Partners and Inter's Oaktree.

The stadium's architects feature a collaboration between Foster+Partners and MANICA, bringing together Lord Norman Foster and David Manica. The two architects previously collaborated on the design of London's Wembley Stadium.

The project will now go through design and planning phase. Construction is expected to begin in 2028 and the first match targeted for the 2031-32 season, subject to the necessary approvals. The project is also part of a broader urban regeneration plan for the area that will include public spaces, green areas as well as leisure and retail spaces.

According to a joint news release from both clubs, the design is inspired by "the intricate craftsmanship of the Duomo di Milano." Two seating tiers will form a continuous 360-degree bowl.

Originally built in 1926, the San Siro, with its striking spiral staircases wrapped around the outside of the stadium, was renovated for the 1990 World Cup but lacks the facilities offered by other top European football venues.

At either end, the iconic "Curvas" will rise as single, steep walls, drawing fans forward toward the field of play.

Seating inclinations of up to 37 degrees will amplify both atmosphere and visual impact.

According to the release, the intention is to "bring supporters closer than ever before to the moments that matter most."

AC Milan and Inter Milan bought the land for the stadium off the city last November for €197 million ($230 million), paving the way for its demolition and the construction of a new venue. The two Serie A clubs have long shared the use of the historic ground, but see building a joint modern arena as vital to boosting their matchday revenue, which lags behind their European rivals.

Italy is under growing pressure to upgrade the quality of its stadiums, driven by foreign investors backing Serie A clubs and the need for more functional venues for the 2032 European Championship, which it will co-host with Türkiye.

articles.headline: Debunk or double down? Judging 10 early-season NBA overreactions
articles.description: A 29-year-old is the NBA's next breakout star. Miami's Giannis era is already cooked. And so are the Thunder, Knicks and Warriors. Which overreactions are valid?
articles.headlineJa: 間違いか、それとも確信か？シーズン序盤のNBAにおける10の過剰反応を検証
articles.descriptionJa: 29歳の選手がNBAの次なるブレイクスターになる。マイアミのヤニス時代はすでに終わっている。サンダー、ニックス、ウォリアーズも同様だ。どの過剰反応が妥当だろうか？
articles.body:
Welcome to the final days of October, featuring falling leaves, early sunsets, Halloween decorations illuminating the night -- and the yearly pastime of overreacting to the first week of a new NBA season.

After all, small sample size theatre has provided early gems such as:

The sky is falling in Oklahoma City, New York and Miami!

The three-guard experiment in San Antonio needs to go!

Charlotte is already better without LaMelo Ball!

Ty Jerome? Ty Jerome!

With those early storylines and more in mind, let's examine 10 popular overreactions to the young 2026-27 season -- and determine which have staying power. (Note: stats through Tuesday's games.)

The Miami Heat will finish with their worst record since 2008.

Zach Kram: Not an overreaction

For reference, 2007-08 was the last time the Heat finished with fewer than 37 wins, the season that they tanked down the stretch to go 15-67 in a futile attempt to land Derrick Rose in the draft.

Merely by the law of averages, the 2026-27 Heat are bound to improve. They've had the seventh-worst shooting luck on offense, according to GeniusIQ tracking, and the second-worst shooting luck on defense. Miami is actually forcing teams into tough shots, but its opponents have been on fire regardless, making 53% of their midrange shots and 40% of their 3s, per Cleaning the Glass.

On the other hand, the Heat's offense has been stuck in the mud even accounting for that poor shooting luck, and guard Davion Mitchell is the only role player who looks comfortable playing with Giannis Antetokounmpo. There's time for that to change -- but as of Wednesday, ESPN's Basketball Power Index predicts the Heat will finish the season with just 38 wins. That's already down from 46 projected wins in the preseason, and just one ahead of this historical franchise benchmark.

Ben Golliver: Overreaction

Let's be clear: The Antetokounmpo era in South Beach is off to an atrocious start. Instead of building off its blockbuster trade for the two-time MVP with a transformative offseason, the Heat lost Norman Powell to the Chicago Bulls in free agency and settled for adding Klay Thompson, who is a shell of his former self at age 36. On the court, it's already clear that the Heat need another proven ball handler and more shooting, and Antetokounmpo needs more time to jell with Bam Adebayo.

Despite all those challenges, it's reasonable to give Heat coach Erik Spoelstra and his staff a long runway. Antetokounmpo's need to dominate the ball has clashed with the free-flowing offensive system that Miami utilized in 2025-26, and several veteran players seem to be easing into the new season. Spoelstra is a tinkerer who has conjured winning records from less talented rosters, and he'll be willing to trust his younger options if Miami's offensive struggles persist.

articles.headline: Timberwolves' Anthony Edwards undergoes successful knee scope
articles.description: Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards underwent a "successful" arthroscopic procedure on his ailing right knee at the Mayo Clinic on Thursday, the team announced.
articles.headlineJa: ティンバーウルブズのアンソニー・エドワーズ、膝の関節鏡手術に成功
articles.descriptionJa: ティンバーウルブズのスター、アンソニー・エドワーズが木曜日にメイヨークリニックで不調だった右膝の関節鏡手術を受け、成功したことをチームが発表した。
articles.body:
Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards underwent a "successful" arthroscopic procedure on his ailing right knee at the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minn. on Thursday, the team announced.

Edwards had a debridement procedure performed on his knee, which is a minimally invasive measure used to clean, smooth, or remove damaged cartilage, bone spurs, or loose joint fragments from the knee joint to relieve pain and improve mobility, according to the Mayo Clinic.

The team's statement said Edwards is expected to make a full recover but did not denote a timeframe for his potential return. Sources tell ESPN's Shams Charania that Edwards could be sidelined up to two months.

Speaking before Wednesday night's loss to the Warriors, Timberwolves president of basketball operations Tim Connelly said he expects Edwards to be "good as new" when he eventually returns to game action.

Edwards has been bothered by right knee pain since last spring and was limited to a career-low 61 games last season. He was seen grabbing his knee and grimacing at one point during Sunday's home opener against the Toronto Raptors. Even after being listed as questionable to play Monday, Edwards scored 47 points in an overtime loss at Cleveland. His 133 points through four games is a franchise record.

An MRI on Tuesday revealed new damage for Edwards that was not detected in previous scans, which were done before training camp and during the playoffs. His condition this summer was not such that a procedure would have been recommended then, Connelly said Wednesday.

"We're just concerned about his long-term health," Connelly added. "We want to make sure we're putting him in the best position he can be so he can be the best version he's going to be for a long time.

"He's bummed, but Anthony is such a naturally positive and upbeat guy. He's hit all his teammates quickly and said, 'You guys got it,' and we'll roll from there."

Wolves coach Chris Finch said before Wednesday's loss to Golden State that the Edwards news was "a bit of a shock to everybody." Finch, however, feels confident that his team has the depth and experience to navigate an extended stretch without Edwards.

"We'll have to kind of fill that scoring void by committee," Finch said. "Certainly, spreading more shots around the team, everybody likes that. Obviously they've got to go in to make up the point difference."

Information from the Associated Press was used in this report.

articles.headline: PSG's Luis Enrique: Vitinha deserved higher Ballon d'Or ranking
articles.description: Paris Saint-Germain boss Luis Enrique does not believe star midfielder Vitinha got the recognition he deserved in the Ballon d'Or rankings.
articles.headlineJa: PSGのルイス・エンリケ監督、ヴィティーニャはバロンドールでより高い順位にふさわしかったと主張
articles.descriptionJa: パリ・サンジェルマンのルイス・エンリケ監督は、スターミッドフィルダーのヴィティーニャがバロンドールのランキングで正当な評価を得られたと考えていない。
articles.body:
Paris Saint-Germain boss Luis Enrique does not believe star midfielder Vitinha got the recognition he deserved in the Ballon d'Or rankings.

The back-to-back Champions League winners head to rock-bottom Le Havre on Friday evening having moved top of Ligue 1 with last weekend's 2-0 win against Lyon.

PSG return to action fresh from being crowned Men's Club of the Year at the 70th Ballon d'Or ceremony, when 10 of their players were among the 30 nominees for the men's award.

Vitinha was among those and ended up 14th, a year on from finishing third when team-mate Ousmane Dembélé lifted the trophy.

PSG boss Enrique said of the Portugal international: "It's a real pleasure to have a player with such technical and physical ability. His level is incredible.

"We're very pleased to have a player of his calibre, even though he wasn't ranked as highly as he deserves to be in the Ballon d'Or rankings."

Sixth-placed Khvicha Kvaratskhelia was PSG's highest-ranked player at the Ballon d'Or and this week underwent surgery in Qatar on a torn anterior cruciate ligament.

Dembélé finished seventh and is another missing for Friday's game at Le Havre, as are Nuno Mendes and Marquinhos after recording 23rd and 25th place finishes.

PSG said the trio "all continue their rehabilitation" and head coach Enrique said: "We like to have as much control as possible, and the issue of injuries has been a major focus of our work in recent years.

"Some players suffer injuries more frequently than others, so it can sometimes be difficult to control. We aim to refine and optimise the training load to minimise the number of injured players.

"Throughout my coaching career, we've always sought to manage this; there have been tough times and better times, but I'm pleased with what we're trying to achieve.

"However, it's always difficult because injuries are part and parcel of top-flight football."

PSG have the strength in depth to cope, even with a Champions League match at Villarreal and home game against Troyes following the perennial Ligue 1 champions' game at winless Le Havre.

Enrique knows the pressure is on them to stay in their "favourite position" and wants to continue building as they head to the Stade Océane seeking a ninth straight win in all competitions.

ESPN's basketball daily cheat sheet is your pregame destination before you lock in daily fantasy and betting decisions for that night's games. Here you'll find our top insights for the slate, including players to target for your daily fantasy rosters, along with game-by-game injury reports.

What you need to know for Thursday

Thursday's NBA schedule has just three games, but there are some interesting matchups. Two undefeated teams meet in Portland, two winless teams face off in New Orleans, and the Cleveland Cavaliers and Atlanta Hawks are both playing on the second night of a back-to-back.

The Cavaliers (3-1) have won three straight heading into their matchup against the Hawks (2-3). Evan Mobley finished with 24 points and 12 rebounds in Wednesday's win over Washington, while Peyton Watson added 22 points. The Hawks, meanwhile, have lost three consecutive games despite strong early-season production from Jalen Johnson.

The Sacramento Kings (0-4) and New Orleans Pelicans (0-4) are both looking for their first win. Zach LaVine has averaged 27.3 points per game for Sacramento. Zion Williamson and the Pelicans will be playing their second game in as many nights.

articles.headline: Crystal Palace's Ismaïla Sarr set to be sidelined for weeks, Pierre Sage confirms
articles.description: Ismaïla Sarr is likely to remain sidelined with a groin issue until after the international break, Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage has confirmed.
articles.headlineJa: クリスタル・パレスのイスマイラ・サール、数週間の離脱へ。ピエール・サージュが認める
articles.descriptionJa: クリスタル・パレスのピエール・サージュ監督は、イスマイラ・サールが鼠径部の問題により、代表ウィーク明けまで戦線を離脱する可能性が高いことを認めた。
articles.body:
Ismaïla Sarr is likely to remain sidelined with a groin issue until after the international break, Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage has confirmed.

The Senegal international was last season's Conference League top scorer, but has made just five appearances for Palace across all competitions so far.

Palace have lost one of those five games, while they have been beaten in five of the eight matches he has missed, but the under-pressure Sage will have to do without him for at least the next three outings before the November international window.

When asked about when the 28-year-old might be available again, Sage said: "I think after the international break."

The under-pressure Eagles boss secured a big Carabao Cup win at Fulham on Wednesday night, and will now look to turn Palace's Premier League fortunes around at Tottenham before hosting Hoffenheim in the Europa League, then welcoming Liverpool to Selhurst Park before the pause.

Asked if he might prefer to be taking on their subsequent league opponents -- Coventry and Hull -- Sage said: "Every point smells good, and if we take points against Liverpool or Tottenham or against the other team, it's the same for us at the end, because we need, and we will play all the game to take points.

"We are not in a position to choose one game better than another. We do, we did, and we will do the same with the cups and the league too. That's why we made some rotations, because we wanted to win on Wednesday, but we wanted to create the conditions of freshness for Saturday too.

"At the moment that strategy is good, but we have to confirm that and go until the goal we fixed at the beginning of the week."

Sage confirmed Jean-Philippe Mateta was rested against Fulham but will be ready to start against Tottenham.

Jorgen Strand Larsen continues to recover from the ankle issue he sustained in their 2-2 draw with Besiktas last week, and will train with the group on Thursday afternoon.

Sage confirmed Quinten Timber could also potentially feature in the Spurs clash, which should also feature captain Dean Henderson who recovered well on his first start back from injury on Wednesday.

Palace sit one place and point clear of the relegation zone heading into Sunday's trip to north London, and there has been some suggestion that this weekend could be a major test of the front office's faith that Sage remains the right man for the job.

articles.headline: Man City, Bayern among the good, bad and lucky in Europe's top leagues
articles.description: We're a quarter of the way through the 2026-27 European season -- long enough to separate fact from fiction when it comes to from. Who's been lucky? Who's been good? Who's been both, or neither?
articles.body:
About a quarter of the way through the club season, your place in the table only means so much. In the Premier League and Bundesliga, 14 teams -- including Ipswich Town, Paderborn and even Tottenham Hotspur -- are within six points of the top four. In Ligue 1, it's 13. In LaLiga, 14 teams are within six points of the relegation zone. You can find some separation here and there, but we're just getting started, and we only have a partial picture of how things will end up.

We also know that the table is lying a little bit. We see funky results all the time, and they have an outsized impact when we're seen only a small portion of matches. Still, by this point in the 2026-27 campaign, each Big Five team has played hundreds and hundreds of possessions, and we know who is creating (or allowing) the best chances. Thanks to xG, we also know what that means.

Essentially, xG is a chance creation metric. It obviously doesn't guarantee success, especially in the short term, but over the long haul a team's ability to create superior shot quality and/or volume is more predictive than simply who's putting the ball in the net in a small sample. And by comparing who's generated the most points to who's created chance creation advantages, with a fun trend line in between, we can get a grasp of who is ahead of or behind where they should be.

Who's both lucky and good? Who's good, but unlucky? Who's the opposite?

Here are some xG standouts, for better or worse, in Europe's Big Five leagues.

- Jones: Vozinha's Ballon d'Or appearance was made for us

- Ogden: Man United are a mess. Where are the Glazers?

- Olley: Ballon d'Or is Kane's crowning moment

Lucky and good

Definition: Teams with an xG differential of at least +0.3 per game, but more points than expected

Lazio. Lazio have finished seventh or worse in Serie A for three straight years, and due to an ongoing fan protest of club president Claudio Lotito, they're averaging a league-worst home attendance of 9,515. They've also only dropped two points in nine league matches, and they're tied with Inter atop the table. Pretty wild stuff.

It's also probably unsustainable stuff.

While they've enjoyed a few genuinely dominant performances (like a 6-2 win at Sassuolo), they've also scored 22 goals from shots worth just 15.5 xG. Forward Tijjani Noslin, winger Gustav Isaksen and midfielder Kenneth Taylor have combined for nine goals from 3.9 xG; I probably don't have to spell out how unsustainable that is. Lazio have stockpiled enough points to remain in the Champions League hunt for a while, but there's a goal-scoring slump in their future, whether or not there are fans in the stands to see it.

Atletico Madrid. Diego Simeone scoffs at your advanced stats. Over the past 12 full seasons, Atletico have produced a goal differential higher -- and in some cases, much higher -- than their xG differential 11 times. articles.headline: Michael Carrick: 'Not surprised' to still be Man United manager
articles.description: Michael Carrick said he is "not surprised" to still be in a job as Manchester United manager, despite the team failing to win any of its past eight games.
articles.body:
Michael Carrick said he is "not surprised" to still be in a job as Manchester United manager, despite the team failing to win any of its past eight games and making its worst league start for 40 years.

Carrick, who signed a two-year contract this summer after guiding United into the Champions League following his arrival as a short-term successor to Ruben Amorim in January, had been expected to lose his job this week following a 3-0 home defeat against Bournemouth on Sunday.

But after a series of meetings involving the United hierarchy on Monday, Carrick has been left in charge for Saturday's Premier League trip to Chelsea.

And when asked whether he was surprised to still be in a job, the former United midfielder said he is ready to continue in his role.

"No, I am here to do my job and do my job for the team," Carrick said in response to a question as to whether he was surprised to still be at the club. "I'm desperate to make us better and improve things, so I'm not surprised, no.

"I said after the [Bournemouth] game that I didn't expect anything. I was dealing with the performance and the result.

"There was no hiding that the dynamics in the stadium were a bit different from normal. My mind was going through that and digesting that as I mentioned to [the media] after the game.

"It was purely that my mind was [thinking] 'what do we need to do to improve things?'"

Despite the lengthy talks and delay in the club communicating that Carrick would remain in charge, the 45-year-old said he has not sought assurances from the hierarchy about his job.

"I don't need any assurances from anyone," he said. "I totally get the position, get the job, the responsibilities and what comes with that.

"I care what the supporters think, what it feels like in the stadium. I genuinely don't take any notice of anything else. I know this job and what it brings."

articles.headline: Michael Carrick: Bruno Fernandes retains Man United captaincy
articles.description: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick said Bruno Fernandes will keep the team's captaincy, despite his decision to drop the midfielder for their 3-0 defeat vs. Bournemouth.
articles.body:
Manchester United manager Michael Carrick said Bruno Fernandes will keep the team's captaincy, despite his decision to drop the Portugal midfielder for their 3-0 defeat against Bournemouth on Sunday for outspoken comments about the team's tactics.

Carrick has held on to his job following discussions involving the club hierarchy this week, despite an eight-game winless run and the team's worst start to a league season since 1986.

And the former Middlesbrough manager confirmed Fernandes will return to the starting lineup and retain the captaincy against Chelsea on Saturday after remaining on the bench against Bournemouth.

Carrick handed Harry Maguire the captain's armband in Sunday's loss.

"There is no decision to be made on [the captaincy]," Carrick said. "It will be Bruno. Listen, we're clear with the situation of the team and as a football club at the moment. He's an important player for this group. He has been and he will be.

"Between us, we've got to make a difference and we've got to push things in a good direction. He's fully committed to this football club, he's fully committed to making things better. It doesn't change for me. He's the one that's kind of led the team so well for many a game and many a year, and he'll continue to do that."

Kobbie Mainoo could return to the squad for the trip to Chelsea after training this week following a recent layoff, but Carrick said that striker Benjamin Sesko faces an extended layoff with a shin injury. Sesko has not played since the Carabao Cup defeat against Brighton on Sept. 16 and is now expected to be out until the New Year.

"Ben looks like he's going to be out for a period of time," Carrick said. "We're still not clear of exactly how long, but it's going to be for a longer period of time. It was the process and we had to go through the process. There's a bit of a healing process for the injury to see how it would react and what direction to go with that.

"So even now we're still working through it. But yeah, it's unfortunate, obviously first and foremost for Ben, for the kind of period that he's had and tried to get through it."

articles.headline: Fantasy basketball: Seven preseason assumptions already being challenged
articles.description: The fantasy basketball experts go over what hasn't gone as planned during the opening week of the NBA season.
articles.body:
Sometimes, it takes a while to see how the things are going to shake out in this new NBA season. Other times, it is plainly obvious that things are not as they seemed before the season officially tipped off, whether that means less playing time, a drop in production, or changes under a new coaching staff.

With that in mind, we asked our fantasy basketball experts Andre Snellings, Eric Moody, Eric Karabell, Steve Alexander, Jim McCormick and Michael F. Florio to identify the biggest preseason assumptions that are already being challenged.

Here's what has stood out to them after one week of NBA action.

Tyrese Maxey, other 76ers thriving despite Philadelphia's star power

Moody: The concern in Philadelphia was that too many stars would eat into Maxey's production. LeBron James and Jaylen Brown joined Joel Embiid, but Maxey averaged 50 fantasy points per game through four games as the Sixers opened 3-1. Brown contributed 36.0 fantasy points per game, and Embiid recorded a 28-point triple-double against the Milwaukee Bucks last Saturday. There will be nights when someone sacrifices touches, but Maxey hasn't looked like the player making that sacrifice.

Florio: While LeBron and Embiid have already missed a game and that was a big fear, they have performed extremely well so far, especially in Roto formats. Maxey is a Top 5 player in all formats, while Embiid and Brown are each averaging over 20 PPG. LeBron James continues to contribute across the board. It's still early, but fading them in fantasy is one early season regret.

Giannis' arrival is already affecting Adebayo's production

Karabell: Perhaps I hadn't considered the potential statistical downside of what superstar Giannis Antetokoumpo joining the Miami Heat would mean for longtime underrated star Bam Adebayo. So far, the fit looks awkward. Adebayo averaged 20.1 PPG and 10 RPG last season, continuing a seven-season run of excellence. Is that over now? Bam is off to a terrible start (11.8 PPG, 7.3 RPG, 40% FG, 61.5% FT), and oh, Miami is winless. These numbers must improve, but how much? Is Bam still a top 50 fantasy option? Maybe so, maybe not.

Alex Sarr will have to wait to reach new heights

Snellings: Sarr is unlikely to approach, let alone build on, his breakout campaign from last season if the Washington Wizards are fully healthy. After averaging 16.3 PPG, 7.4 RPG and 2.0 BPG last season, he is currently averaging 8.8 PPG, 5.3 RPG and 1.3 BPG in this one. With Anthony Davis occupying all the spaces Sarr prefers but at much higher volume, Sarr just doesn't have the shots (6.5 FGA this season, down from 13.7 FGA last year), rebounding or shot-blocking opportunities to approach what he did last season. And number one overall pick AJ Dybantsa hasn't even played yet this season, so once he's in the fold Sarr may get even fewer looks.
